verdict.line: You out-trade and out-kill Nasus through the laning phase on the back of your engage tools, but if the game drags past the point his Siphoning Strike stacks and Fury of the Sands drain compound, the matchup flattens back to even.

brief.thesis: Nasus's whole kit is short-range and has zero mobility outside of Wither's slow, while Aatrox's W (825 range) and E (dash) let you pick exactly when every fight happens. The 51.6% head-to-head win rate and Aatrox's lane/solo-kill edge both come from this gap during the early-mid game; it only closes once Nasus's Q stacks and Fury of the Sands drain start making up for his lack of mobility.

theirWindow.what: Wither decelerates your Movement and Attack Speed for its duration with no counterplay once it hits; disengage immediately with E (Umbral Dash) instead of trading through it, since a slowed extended trade lets his Soul Eater lifesteal and stacked Q damage win the exchange.

yourWindow.when: Level 3, once W and E are up
yourWindow.what: Open with W (Infernal Chains, 825 range) to drag him in from outside his 255-range Q, then follow with Q (The Darkin Blade) swings and E (Umbral Dash) for the on-hit heal. Repeat this every time your cooldowns reset, since Nasus has no dash or escape to answer it.

start.why: Highest-winrate, most-picked start (51.8% over 3069 games); the extra sustain and damage matter because you're initiating short trades repeatedly, and Nasus's own early sustain from Soul Eater is weak until he stacks Q.

boots.why: Best-performing boots in the matchup (54.7% over 1195 games); the tenacity directly cuts the duration of Wither's slow, which is the only tool Nasus has to stop you disengaging or re-engaging on your terms.

core.why: First item in the highest-winrate recorded path (66.3% over 101 games); the shield and burst reward you for landing full W-into-Q-into-E combos in short trades.
Second item in that same 66.3% path; the ability haste lets you loop W/E engages faster, which matters since your whole advantage is forcing fights before he scales.
Shows up as the third item across every recorded core path (53.8%-66.3%); the damage-over-time conversion keeps you alive through Nasus's stacked Q burst once his items come online.

runes.keystoneWhy: The highest-winrate, highest-pickrate page (52.2%, 35.3% pick) runs Conqueror, and it rewards exactly the repeated short melee trades you're forcing every time your W/E come off cooldown.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked (84.1%) and highest-winrate (52.6%) combo; Ignite directly cuts into Nasus's Soul Eater lifesteal during your early all-ins and converts your existing solo-kill advantage into actual kills.

playing.title: Engage from outside his Q range
playing.detail: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike) only reaches 255 range. Use W (Infernal Chains, 825 range) to drag him to you before he can land a safe stack, rather than letting him poke you first.

playing.title: Use every cooldown after level 3
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to stop letting Nasus farm stacks uncontested the moment you hit level 3 — fire W and E on cooldown to force fights instead of waiting for a perfect engage.

playing.title: Time all-ins around Deathbringer Stance
playing.detail: Your passive periodically empowers your next auto with bonus magic damage and healing based on the target's max health; hold the all-in a beat if the proc isn't up, since it swings short trades hard in your favor.

playing.title: Step off Spirit Fire immediately
playing.detail: Nasus's E (Spirit Fire, 12s cooldown, 650 range) reduces the armor of anyone standing in it. Don't stand and trade inside the flame — exit the zone instead of letting the armor shred stack.

playing.title: Disengage the instant Wither lands
playing.detail: Wither (W, 700 range) decelerates both your Movement and Attack Speed for its duration with no way to shake it off; use E (Umbral Dash) to get out rather than trading through a slow you can't win.

playing.title: Respect both ultimates coming online together
playing.detail: Aatrox's R (World Ender) and Nasus's R (Fury of the Sands) share the same level-6 timing. Bait his Fury of the Sands away from minions before you commit, or use your own fear-and-heal window to force the fight on your terms.

playing.title: Close the lane out, don't let it drag
playing.detail: Your edge is real but front-loaded — convert your lane and solo-kill advantage into a gold or tempo lead in the first two back trips, because Nasus's Q stacks and Fury drain compound the longer the game runs.

brief.patchCaveat: The win rates, build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG. The tactical reasoning — how to use the W/E engage window, when to respect Wither, and how to time the level-6 ultimates — is my own analysis layered on top of that data, not sourced from it.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow by using your skills after reaching level 3 to gain lane control. Use your skills whenever they come off cooldown to engage often.
